result.title: Calibrated Disambiguation for Partial Multi-label Learning
result.comment: The paper is accepted by AAAI 2025
result.summary: Partial multi-label learning (PML) aims to train a classifier on datasets whose instances are over-annotated with not only relevant labels but also irrelevant labels, which is common when datasets are collected from crowd-sourcing platform. Existing works primarily approach it from a curriculum learning perspective, leveraging the memorization effect to disambiguate noisy labels and produce robust predictions. However, these methods are based on non-adaptive weighting functions and lack theoretical guidance for optimal weighting. To overcome these issues, a calibrated disambiguation model named PML-CD is proposed. We first formulate the optimal weighting function for curriculum-based disambiguation, which is equivalent to the calibration of the model's predicted confidences, thus providing guidance for curriculum designing. To obtain the optimal weighting function from PML dataset during the training, a transferable calibrator is designed, which takes the histogram of positive samples' confidences as input, and outputs the optimal curriculum weighting for training. Prototype alignment regularization is also proposed to promote the model's performance. Experiments conducted on Pascal VOC, MS-COCO, NUS-WIDE and CUB have verified that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art PML methods.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对部分多标签学习中的过标注噪声，提出 PML-CD：把基于课程学习的最优加权函数形式化为对模型预测置信度的校准，并用一个以正样本置信度直方图为输入的校准器在训练中生成课程权重，辅以原型对齐正则。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「由置信度分布学习自适应权重」的校准思路，可能为 LVR 中潜在步骤的加权、监督贡献分配或基于置信度的停止/核验提供可核查的方法线索，但原文任务为噪声标签去歧义，与视觉推理状态无直接关系，需人工判断迁移价值。
